whatItIs: A fixed set of constructed record pairs with the classification each one should receive, written from the comparison's specification before the candidate was run against any of them.
whatItIsNot: Not a measured accuracy rate. Every pair here is built by the same engine from synthetic inputs, so this measures whether the comparison classifies the cases its rules describe. It says nothing about how often the tool is right about a disagreement between two independently authored astrology engines, and nothing about real-world users, because no such corpus exists here.
inputs: Synthetic throughout: round coordinates for well-known cities, and dates chosen for what they exercise. No real person's birth details.

scenarios.purpose: The same record twice must report nothing, and must not manufacture an explanation for nothing.
Placidus against whole sign in an ordinary place: every cusp moves, no body and no angle moves, and the cause is demonstrable by recalculating one side.
The same moment written 13:30Z and 19:00+05:30. Only how it was written differs; nothing computed may differ, and the cause is read off the files rather than guessed.
A known birth time against an unknown one. The bodies are the same instant either way; the angles, the houses and the cusps are absent on one side, and an absent birth time accounts for all three.

explanationStatementExcludes.pattern: different one was actually used|asked for different house systems

scenarios.purpose: Two charts two days either side of the vernal equinox, with the Sun at 359.19 degrees and 1.18 degrees. Those are two degrees apart around the circle; a subtraction would call them 358 apart.

A record claiming engine 99.0.0 against one from the pinned engine, with a real house-system difference between them. The obvious cause must stay a hypothesis: recalculating a 99.0.0 record on the pinned engine is a different calculation, not the original, and the limit must say so by naming both versions.

A different house system and a different hour at once. The house system moves cusps and cannot move a body, so its explanation must claim no body row — the direction of over-claim that a does-any-input-differ test gets wrong.

Two different places and two different moments at once. Several causes fit and none is demonstrable; the tool must offer them all and state that it cannot separate their contributions rather than picking one.

expect.limitsMatch: moment and the place both differ

scenarios.required: a requested house system that was not the one used
scenarios.purpose: Placidus and whole sign both requested at 78 degrees north, where Placidus falls back to whole. The requested systems differ and not one cusp moves, so nothing was reproduced and reproduced must not be claimed: matching values that never moved demonstrates nothing.

scenarios.required: a difference smaller than the printed precision
scenarios.purpose: Two calculations six milliseconds apart. Some values move far enough to print differently at six decimals and some do not, and the smallest real difference is smaller than the largest rounding one — so no tolerance on distance could separate them, which is why the verdict is decided on what is printed.

scenarios.required: a receipt naming an engine this installation does not have, whose values nevertheless match
scenarios.purpose: The second record's values are exactly what the installed engine produces, and its receipt says they came from an engine nobody here has. Reproducing them locally is then a fact about this engine, not a demonstration about why these two files differ — so the cause must stay a hypothesis, and the same verdict must come back whichever file is passed first.

scenarios.required: equal SemVer precedence, different build and provenance claims
scenarios.purpose: SemVer ignores build metadata when ordering versions, and this module says the same: a differently labelled build is not a different engine and must not be refused a replay as if it were. Neither claim is authenticated, so neither can grant or withhold a verdict. It is recorded in `limits`, where an unauthenticated assertion belongs, while the verdict rests on each record's own values reproducing from its own declared inputs.

expect.limitsMatch: each claims a different build of it

scenarios.required: equal precedence and the same build claim on both sides
scenarios.purpose: The control for the case above. Two receipts naming the same build, metadata included, have told this tool nothing about their provenance either — but they have not told it they differ, so the ordinary demonstration still stands and withholding here would be the opposite error.

scenarios.required: a record whose values do not follow from the inputs it declares
scenarios.purpose: A genuine 14:30 chart with its declared instant rewritten to 13:30. The parser accepts it, because it checks internal coherence rather than that a result follows from its inputs. Without reproducing each record's own values from its own declared inputs first, the comparison called this pair reproduced while the house system explained none of it.

expect.limitsMatch: could not be reproduced from the inputs it declares

scenarios.required: the default response still carries the diagnosis
scenarios.purpose: The same pair as `wraparound`, read from the default response instead of the full one. The absolute longitudes are withheld there because a body longitude is a computed position; the signed circular difference is not, because that is what tells a caller what moved and by how much. This is the scenario that keeps the privacy default from quietly gutting the answer.

scenarios.required: a rewritten instant that the cusps alone cannot detect
scenarios.purpose: The counterexample that forced the baseline to widen. Whole-sign cusps are quantised to sign boundaries, so they survive an hour of drift in the declared instant without moving. A baseline checking the cusps alone passes trivially here, and the pair reached the strongest verdict in the vocabulary while sixty-five rows sat unresolved. The angles and body longitudes move continuously, which is what makes them the discriminating evidence.

expect.limitsMatch: could not be reproduced from the inputs it declares

scenarios.required: a rewritten place, reached the same way as a rewritten moment
scenarios.purpose: The same hole through the coordinates. A chart genuinely computed three degrees east, declaring the London longitude, with whole-sign houses on the drifted side so the cusps again cannot tell.

expect.limitsMatch: could not be reproduced from the inputs it declares

scenarios.required: one receipt claiming a build and the other claiming none
scenarios.purpose: A file that says nothing about its build has not said something different from one that does. The first attempt at this audit compared the two as strings, refused the replay, and described the pair in a sentence that was false. The difference is still reported by the cause that owns it.

amendments.after: the candidate had already been run against the original plan
amendments.why: A bounded AI review found the comparison naming the house system as "the obvious candidate for the angle differences" in this exact pair. A house system cannot move an angle — the ascendant and midheaven come from the time and the place — so that was a hypothesis a recalculation refutes, and the original guard could not catch it because it forbade only body rows. Fixing it also removed the reason nothing here reached "reproduced": promotion had been blocked by requiring the replay to reproduce angles the house system never moved. With that gone the house-system cause is demonstrated for this pair, and an assertion that nothing may be demonstrated would be asserting the defect. Recorded rather than quietly edited: this is a post-hoc change to a pre-registered plan, and the strengthened guard is the assertion that actually matches the scenario purpose.

amendments.after: the candidate had already been run against the original plan
amendments.why: The same review found this pair reported as "The same house system was requested, but a different one was actually used" when both sides requested placidus and one simply had no house table. The original expectations checked coverage and evidence rank but nothing about what a statement says, so a reader could be told the systems disagreed. The rows still need a claimant, so the fix corrected the sentence and kept the coverage, and this assertion pins it.

amendments.after: an audit of the shared reproduced contract
amendments.added: four scenarios (foreign-engine-but-matching-values, different-build-claims, same-build-claims, drifted-baseline) and an orderIndependent structural check on every scenario
amendments.why: The audit asked whether a recalculation can be called a demonstrated cause without establishing that it is entitled to speak for both records. It can, three ways, and each is now a scenario: the other receipt naming an engine nobody here has, the two receipts claiming different builds of the same version, and a record whose values do not follow from the inputs it declares. The fourth, same-build-claims, is the control that keeps the fix from being an over-correction. No previous expectation was weakened or removed; the ten original scenarios and their 59 assertions are unchanged and still pass. The orderIndependent flag adds an assertion rather than replacing one: the same two files reaching different verdicts depending on which was passed first was itself one of the findings.

amendments.after: the comparison tool's default response stopped repeating birth details and positions back
amendments.added: compareOutput: "full" on `wraparound`, and a new scenario reading the same pair from the default response
amendments.why: `rowValuesStraddleZero` inspects the two absolute longitudes, to show the pair really does straddle 0 degrees rather than merely having a small difference. The default response withholds those values now, because a body longitude is a computed position. The assertion is unchanged and still runs — the scenario simply states which response it reads. The new scenario covers the case the change created: that the default still names the row and carries its signed circular difference. Requesting the full response for one scenario is not a weakening; asserting the straddle against a response that does not contain it would have been.

amendments.after: a bounded AI review of the corrected reproduced contract
amendments.removed: explanationEvidence: house-system = hypothesis, and limitsMatch "claim different builds of it"
amendments.added: explanationEvidence: house-system = reproduced, limitsMatch "each claims a different build of it"; and the scenarios quantised-cusps-drift, drifted-place and one-sided-build-claim
amendments.why: This reverses an expectation registered one day earlier, so the reason has to carry the weight. The first correction made a differing build claim refuse the replay outright. The review showed that contradicted the rule already written in diff.ts — build metadata does not make a different engine and must not be refused a replay as if it were — and contradicted the response itself, which printed "build metadata does not change which version a receipt was produced by" beside a limit saying the two claims made the replay unusable. It also treated a record claiming nothing as claiming something different, which is simply false. The audit's own instruction is not to infer authentic provenance from a version or checksum supplied inside a receipt; that cuts both ways, so the claim now goes to limits and the verdict rests on evidence this installation can gather. What replaced it is stronger, not weaker: the same review found the cusps-only baseline defeated by whole-sign quantisation, letting a record with a rewritten instant reach "reproduced". quantised-cusps-drift and drifted-place pin that hole shut from both directions, and one-sided-build-claim pins the false-sentence case. Recorded rather than quietly edited.

amendments.after: the candidate had been run against the plan on engine 0.1.1-rc.15
amendments.added: right.utc 1990-06-15T13:30:00.006Z, and "six milliseconds" for "ten" in the purpose
amendments.why: Engine rc.15 reads 1990 as UTC through the leap seconds and UT1 - UTC, and samples the Moon's velocity on a fixed Delta T, so the digits the two charts print moved. Ten milliseconds apart, the smallest real difference, Venus's longitude at 1.36e-7 degrees, is no longer below the largest rounding one, the Venus-Jupiter sextile's orb at 1.11e-7 degrees, and the scenario no longer shows what it exists to show; the assertion failed as written. Six milliseconds apart it does again: the Venus-Saturn trine's orb differs by 8.6e-8 degrees and prints differently, while the South Node's degree differs by 5.1e-7 and prints the same. The unit test of the same property (src/lib/compare/diff.test.ts) moved to six milliseconds for the same reason. The instant is the only change; the purpose, the other assertions and the rule the scenario tests are unchanged. Recorded rather than quietly edited.
